summary: SSE heartbeat misalignment causes mid-stream stalls and silent reconnect cycles
description: Issue summary: NoteWave reports sessions where SSE streams silently cease emitting meaningful 'data:' events for 10-30s, then the client re-establishes the connection and receives a resumed delta that appears to skip ~5-20 tokens. Impact: Production calls to our hosted endpoint for NoteWave chat feature experience visible stalls in user UI and occasional perceived missing text. Several customer sessions escalated as degraded UX during business hours. Environment: Dedicated tenant running in us-east on dedicated pool, traffic passes through customer edge (CloudFront) into our API Gateway -> NLB -> edge-proxy (nginx) -> streaming runtime.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NoteWave dedicated API key with SSE endpoint /v1/stream?model=rw-instruct-v2-large. 2) Send a long generation prompt (~1200 tokens expected). 3) Observe SSE 'data:' chunks in Chrome with default network/stream buffering. 4) Introduce intermittent simulated packet loss (tc/netem) or enable CloudFront idle keepalive/ttl heuristics to mimic caching/proxy behavior. 5) Watch for a pause ~10-30s with keepalive/ping events present on server logs but client not rendering tokens until reconnect.
expected_behavior: SSE stream should continue emitting and client should render incremental tokens. Heartbeats/pings should not be misinterpreted as stream termination or cause the client to stop processing chunks.
actual_behavior: Client sees heartbeats but stops rendering new 'data:' events; after ~20s the client reconnects and asks for resume_token; server responds with resumed fragments which appear to skip a few tokens and the UI shows a gap. No 5xx errors are logged by gateway; NGINX shows keepalive timeouts and large chunk coalescing in access/error logs.

Diagnostic links: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/streaming-latency?var=session=abc123
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Client/browser or intermediate CDN is buffering small SSE chunks and only flushing on client activity or after an internal coalescing timeout, which leads to perceived stalls while server-side heartbeats keep being generated. Hypothesis 2: Our keepalive/heartbeat framing uses 'event: ping' with minimal payload; some proxies treat these as low-priority and drop/aggregate them. Hypothesis 3: Resume handling expects a tokenized last-offset that mismatches when chunks are buffered and later replayed, leading to small gaps. Initial reproduction validated in a staging environment when CloudFront-style keepalive and chunk coalescing enabled. NGINX config on edge-proxy includes proxy_buffering on by default; disabling proxy_buffering reduced stalls in a test run. Metrics show no 5xx but p95 time between SSE 'data' events increases to ~28s during incidents. Linked #support slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02SUPPORT/p1641
comments: Ava Martinez (Support): Customer reported multiple sessions today between 15:45-17:10 where chat output paused. Provided initial logs and asked for SRE investigation.

Theo Patel (SRE): Reproduced in staging with CloudFront/NGINX settings. Observed proxy_buffering causing delayed flush of chunked responses. Opened a test branch to adjust NGINX chunked_transfer_map and proxy_buffering flags.

Lina Zhou (Client SDK): Noted Chrome vs Safari differences; Chrome appears to process incremental 'data:' more reliably when Transfer-Encoding: chunked and small-chunk flushes are set. Will ship a client-side backoff to reconnect only after explicit idle_timeout + no-heartbeat window.
Theo Patel (SRE): Created quick mitigation to set 'X-Accel-Buffering: no' and adjust proxy_buffer_size for dedicated pool; rolling to 10% of servers in us-east.
Customer (NoteWave): Confirmed reduction in stalls after 10% rollout but still saw 1/40 sessions affected. Requested permanent fix and postmortem.
Support (Ava): Scheduled follow-up call and asked for patch ETA and rollout plan.
root_cause: Interaction between intermediate proxy buffering (proxy_buffering enabled on nginx/edge) and our SSE small-chunk heartbeat pattern. Buffered chunks were coalesced and not flushed promptly, causing client-side idle detection and reconnects. Resume flow did not align token offsets when buffered/merged chunks were later delivered.
resolution: 1) Emergency rollback: set 'X-Accel-Buffering: no' on streaming responses for dedicated tenants behind edge-proxy; disabled proxy_buffering for streaming location. 2) Streaming runtime change: increase minimum chunk size/emit explicit flush markers and include sequence numbers in each 'data:' payload to make resume robust. 3) Client SDK change: detect heartbeats separately and treat them as keepalive (do not trigger reconnect) unless both heartbeat and data inactivity exceed a longer threshold. 4) Deployment plan: patch rolled to 100% in us-east by 2026-03-02 02:00Z. 5) Postmortem: create follow-up ticket to add integration tests for proxy buffering and add Grafana alert for SSE inter-event gaps >10s.
postmortem_tasks: INT-4412: Add integration test for SSE with proxy buffering emulation
INT-4510: Update streaming runtime to include per-chunk seq numbers and flush markers
SUP-33211: Communicate permanent fix and recommended nginx settings to dedicated customers
DOCS-78: Add guidance for customers using CloudFront/NGINX in front of Redwood endpoints
